answer: An archive paying agents to preserve onyx scans, ivory substitutes and pigment records can require a distinct, key-encoded data replica for every reward slot. At unpredictable times, agents must prove possession of sampled blocks before a short deadline. With a sound proof-of-replication scheme, extra names cannot reuse one stored copy: a thousand slots require a thousand replicas, making the attacker buy storage and bandwidth. Deadlines must make regenerating missing replicas uneconomic; ordinary file hashes alone cannot enforce this.
